title: Lawyers are already using AI on client work while the firm cannot reconstruct what happened
job: Let lawyers use AI productively without losing confidentiality, provenance, reviewability or client trust.
trigger: Lawyer uses sanctioned or unsanctioned AI in a client matter.
surfaceComplaint: We have an AI policy, but we still cannot tell what people are doing in real matters.
mechanism: Policy governs tools broadly while risk emerges at task/delegation level. Unsanctioned or opaque use can leave no matter-level audit trail.

economics.painCostNote: Upside is frequent; downside asymmetric due to confidentiality, malpractice and client trust.

buyer.roiLogic: Governance spans expensive labor and high-severity risk.

distribution.acquisition: Start with one sanctioned workflow, not enterprise surveillance.

intervention.notBuildYet: No employee surveillance or replacement of legal judgment.

experiment.success: ≥80% compliant use, zero untraceable sampled outputs, no material slowdown
experiment.kill: controls make AI slower or risk/innovation owners cannot align

claims.text: Thomson Reuters reports 34% of law firm professionals use AI tools their firm has not authorized.
2026 research argues many law-firm policies do not govern which cognitive functions can safely be delegated.
The product unit should be the task/matter decision, not the policy PDF.
